rca_unanticipated: Bank Indonesia surprise rate hike to 5.5% announced mid‑morning
Large net foreign sell of Rp 2.58 trillion (distribution) contrary to the slight net buy forecast
Sharp declines in global crude oil prices (WTI -4.20%, Brent -2.57%)
rca_overestimated: Rupiah volatility risk (brief warned of weakening beyond Rp 17,800/USD, but rupiah actually strengthened to Rp 17,695/USD)
Foreign flow magnitude (brief expected only a small sideways net buy, but actual net sell was massive)
rca_underestimated: Impact of the unexpected BI rate hike on market sentiment and liquidity
Effect of the sudden foreign distribution on the IHSG despite a neutral index signal
rca_info_delay: BI rate hike announcement (released after the 08:30 briefing window)
Labor union demo plans announced later in the day
Global market shock commentary published after the morning brief
rca_inverse_correlation: Brief assumed a stronger rupiah would boost IHSG, yet despite the rupiah strengthening to Rp 17,695/USD, the IHSG closed flat at 6,254.97 (0.0% change). The neutral index result was driven by offsetting forces: bullish currency impact was neutralized by heavy foreign selling and deteriorating commodity prices.
lessons: Ketika indikator rupiah menguat dan tidak ada tekanan nilai tukar, tetapi Bank Indonesia secara mendadak menaikkan suku bunga acuan, maka IHSG tetap datar (0.0%) meski diperkirakan naik.
Ketika briefing memperkirakan aliran asing stagnan, tetapi terjadi penjualan asing besar‑besar (net sell Rp 2,58 triliun), maka IHSG tidak bergerak naik dan tetap netral.
summary: Meskipun briefing memprediksi IHSG netral dengan aliran asing sideways dan mengandalkan penguatan rupiah, kejutan kenaikan suku bunga BI dan penjualan asing besar membuat indeks tetap flat.
